instruction: Please create an SSH user named "emily" with password "SecureEm!ly#2024" on Ubuntu who is only allowed to access the folder "/home/storage1".

result.command: USERNAME="emily"; HOMEDIR="/home/storage1"; PASSWORD="SecureEm!ly#2024"; ./check_password.sh "$USERNAME" "$PASSWORD" && [ "$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6)" = "$HOMEDIR" ] && [ $(stat -c "%A" "$HOMEDIR" | cut -b 3) = "w" ] && echo "Password, home directory, and write permission check passed" || echo "Check failed"

include: Password, home directory, and write permission check passed

metadata.explanation: Task creates SSH user 'emily' with password 'SecureEm!ly#2024' restricted to folder '/home/storage1'. Evaluator verifies: (1) SSH password authentication works, (2) home directory is set to /home/storage1, (3) user has write permission to the folder.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical incomplete coverage: Instruction requires user to be 'only allowed to access' /home/storage1, implying access restriction/jail, but evaluator does not verify this restriction
Evaluator only checks: (1) user exists, (2) password works, (3) home directory is /home/storage1, (4) directory has write permission
Missing verification: User is actually RESTRICTED to that folder (cannot access /tmp, /var, /etc, etc.) via chroot, rbash, or other mechanisms
Write permission check logic issue: Checks directory owner-write bit (stat position 3) but does not verify 'emily' is the actual owner of /home/storage1
Security requirement not verified: A user with home=/home/storage1 can still access other directories unless properly jailed/restricted
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification that user cannot access directories outside /home/storage1 (e.g., test 'ssh emily@localhost ls /tmp' fails or is restricted)
Verify user 'emily' is the owner of /home/storage1: check 'stat -c "%U" /home/storage1' equals 'emily'
Check if user has restricted shell (e.g., /bin/rbash) or is in a chroot jail: verify 'getent passwd emily | cut -d: -f7' or chroot configuration
Test actual access restriction: attempt to cd to /tmp or /var as emily and verify it fails
Alternatively, if 'only allowed to access' means something else in context, clarify the instruction to match what the evaluator checks
